name: E00-baseline-logistic
features: shared_full
rationale: Reference. Every shared block, strongest regularisation-free linear model. Nothing here is new; this is the line to beat.

name: E01-baseline-logistic-C0.1
features: shared_full
rationale: Expect a small win or a null: 28+ mildly collinear columns on 13k rows overfit the walk-forward folds, so stronger L2 should help if overfitting is the binding constraint.

name: E10-drop-home-split
features: no_home_split
rationale: Ablation of the one replicated feature finding. Removing it should COST log loss; if it does not, it was not real.

name: E11-drop-opp-adjusted
features: no_opp_adjusted
rationale: Ablation of the pre-registered null. Expect no change, which confirms the 0.98 correlation reading.

name: E12-drop-sos
features: no_sos
rationale: Ablation of the block that died in replication. Expect no change at five folds too - the artifact was only visible at eight.

name: E13-drop-opp-chars
features: no_opp_chars
rationale: Ablation of the never-read OPP_* columns. Measured +0.00000 as a null, so this should confirm it inside the model.

name: E14-home-split-only
features: home_split_only
rationale: Expect a clear loss: schedule and team form are the bulk of the signal, and removing them should cost far more than any block ablation. This is the control that proves the harness can detect a real feature.

name: E15-schedule-only
features: schedule_only
rationale: Expect a large loss. If this beats E00 the harness is broken.

name: E20-rf-full
features: shared_full
rationale: Expect WORSE log loss than logistic: the data is 13k rows of smooth team-strength signal, and boosting already lost to logistic by a significant interval. RF's axis-aligned splits should suit it even less.

name: E21-histgb-full
features: shared_full
rationale: Expect worse than logistic, consistent with the existing HistGB-vs-logistic measurement of -0.00431 [-0.00601, -0.00255].

name: E22-xgb-full
features: shared_full
rationale: Expect worse than logistic, consistent with the existing XGB measurement of -0.00394 [-0.00557, -0.00229].

name: E30-player-elo
features: shared_full
rationale: Reference for the Elo arm. Identical to E00, so any movement is attributable to the six player-Elo columns and nothing else.

name: E31-drop-player-elo
features: no_player_elo
rationale: The ablation. A player's Elo from TEAM results is largely a measure of the team they play for, so this may simply restate ewm_margin on a different scale - which is why the block is correlated against it BEFORE being scored. Correlations: elo_available 0.16, elo_mean 0.09, elo_top5 0.07 against home_ewm_margin. Low, so new information rather than a rescaling.

name: E32-player-elo-C0.1
features: shared_full
rationale: If the Elo columns add correlated signal, stronger L2 should recover a little of whatever regularisation is being spent on them. Expect a null; recorded so the direction is on the record.

name: E40-gaussian-nb-pca20
features: shared_full
rationale: Named BEST by luke-lite/NBA-Prediction-Modeling (53 stars). A different hypothesis class from every other entry: assumes features are conditionally independent given the class, which is plainly false for correlated team statistics. Expect WORSE than logistic, and worth failing out loud.

name: E41-logistic-pca20
features: shared_full
rationale: rileypsmith reports 80 PCs beating 10. The question here is narrower and testable: does unsupervised compression onto 20 components help, help or hurt versus keeping all 59 columns in the logistic? Expect a null - PCA discards exactly the small-variance columns that a regularised model was about to down-weight anyway.

name: E42-ridge
features: shared_full
rationale: A linear model that is not logistic, as a check that the logistic's advantage is about the loss function rather than about being linear at all. Ridge is worse calibrated than logistic by construction, so expect a higher log loss even if its accuracy is competitive - which is the point of ranking on log loss rather than accuracy.

name: S45-prereg-schedule-followup
hypothesis: The schedule block (7 cols: rest days, back-to-backs, 3-in-4, travel_miles) carries a real, leak-free improvement of about -0.002 nats of log loss; the original measurement (delta -0.00203 [−0.00358, −0.00051], |z| = 2.59) was labelled 'lead, not a finding' because it misses the |z| > 3 bar. This follow-up asks whether 0.41 of |z| is obtainable at higher replication power.
protocol_source: GitHub issue #45 (wippa-studios/Legit-NBA-Predictions), 'Pre-registered follow-up: the schedule block'. Its protocol governs.
instrument: scripts/feature_block_ablation.py --blocks schedule, paired bootstrap (n_boot=2000), delta = loss(full) - loss(minus schedule); negative = block earns its place. Frame: the instrument's own build_feature_frame (67 cols = 59 shared + 8 causal rank), identical to the frame that produced the original -0.00203 measurement (results/feature_block_ablation.json, generated 2026-10-17T13:31Z, before issue #45 was filed).
grid: fold counts {4, 5, 6, 8} x bootstrap seeds {42, 137, 2718, 7, 19} = 20 cells. All cells reported, not the best. Seeds fixed here because the issue names none: 42 = script default, 137/2718 = the documented replication seeds (docs/feature_search.md), 7/19 = arbitrary fixed additions. Note: walk_forward_split and the logistic fit are seed-invariant, so at a fixed fold count delta is identical across seeds by construction and the seed dimension probes bootstrap-CI variability only.
decision_rule_binding: Issue #45: the block 'earns its place' iff it clears |z| > 3 at EVERY fold count tested, with the sign stable across every cell and Bonferroni satisfied. Significance at 5 folds and null at 8 is a FAILURE of the test (the strength-of_schedule precedent). Vocabulary per docs/feature_search.md: 'earns its place' / 'still a lead, does not meet the bar' / 'died in replication'.
decision_rule_secondary: Follow-up task rule, evaluated on the four designated settings (seed 42/5 folds primary; 137/5, 2718/5, 42/8 replication): (a) primary 95% CI excludes zero in the helpful direction (ci_hi < 0) AND |z| > 3; (b) point estimates directionally consistent at all four.

multiplicity_stated_before_running.breakdown: 20 replication-grid looks (4 fold counts x 5 seeds) + 7 decomposition looks (one per schedule column)
multiplicity_stated_before_running.cumulative_with_original_family: original feature-search family counted at 10 looks (README); 10 + 27 = 37 -> 0.05/37 = 0.00135, i.e. |z| ~ 3.00
multiplicity_stated_before_running.project_bar: |z| > 3 (Vandenbruaene et al. 2022) applies on top and is not negotiable

decomposition: Pre-registered here; issue #45 is SILENT on decomposition and its protocol constrains only the block-level claim, so this runs as a labelled supplementary analysis and does NOT enter the verdict. Leave-one-column-out within the schedule block at the primary setting (seed 42, 5 folds), same paired-bootstrap machinery (n_boot=2000). Expectation written before running: rest/back-to-back columns carry the effect, travel_miles does not (the actual-travel block measured null at |z| = 1.02, docs/modeling_exploration.md). Caveat written before running: rest_days, back_to_back and in_3_of_4 are strongly collinear, so leave-one-out will under-attribute each column individually; a column failing to clear alone is not evidence it is inert. Executed through the instrument's own functions (fit_oof / drop_block / paired_bootstrap_delta / classify) WITHOUT touching FEATURE_BLOCKS, because single-column sub-blocks would overlap the 'schedule' block and fail Tests/test_feature_block_ablation.py::test_blocks_do_not_overlap.
deviations_recorded_before_running: Issue #45 pre-registers a 4-fold-count x 5-seed grid; the follow-up task's fallback list of four settings is superseded by it ('If the issue specifies a protocol, follow it exactly'). The four designated settings (42/5, 137/5, 2718/5, 42/8) are a subset of the grid and are reported separately.

Issue #45 says 'Same 43-column frame ... Do not revive the 59-column frame', but the existing instrument has no frame selector: its frame is 67 columns and is the frame the quoted -0.00203 lead was measured on. Changing the frame would require restructuring shared code (out of scope) and would make the follow-up incomparable with the original number. The '43-column' phrase is read as pointing at the canonical E14 model bar (log loss 0.61831), which is reported for reference; the ablation is run on the instrument's own frame, as before.
selection_cost_note: No cell is selected: the decision rule is a conjunction over all 20 cells, so there is no best-of-N. The max |z| over the grid will be reported beside the mean only to show what a cherry-pick would have claimed.

name: S45-verdict
selection_cost: No cell is selected (conjunction rule); the cherry-picked maximum |z| over the 20 cells is shown only to demonstrate that even a best-of-20 pick would fail |z| > 3 and fail Bonferroni 0.05/27 = 0.00185.

decision_issue45: FAILS success criterion: |z| > 3 not reached at ANY fold count (range 2.55-2.76). Not a fold artifact and not a replication death: the point estimate is -0.00204 to -0.00212 in every cell and every CI excludes zero. Per issue #45's own wording this is 'a stable small effect that does not meet the bar'.
decision_task_rule: (a) primary CI excludes zero in the helpful direction: PASS; |z| = 2.60 > 3: FAIL. (b) directional consistency at all four designated settings: PASS. Net: FAIL -> 'still a lead'.
verdict: still a lead - stable small effect, below the bar; the block stays in the canonical frame and the README line must read exactly this
decomposition_summary: home_back_to_back -0.00079 [−0.00137,−0.00023] |z| 2.71 is the only column whose interval excludes zero; away_back_to_back -0.00092 leans the same way but straddles zero (|z| 1.61); both rest_days and both in_3_of_4 are nulls with point estimates ~0; travel_miles is a null (|z| 0.46) as pre-registered. No column clears Bonferroni 0.00185 or |z| > 3. LOO shares do not sum to the block effect because the columns are collinear.

name: H3-prereg-recalibration
experiment_type: post-hoc recalibration of the canonical model (theory dossier H3)
hypothesis: Season-blocked, strictly causal recalibration of the canonical model's out-of-fold probabilities - isotonic, Platt, and a regime-aware home-term shrink (home-court advantage measurably shrank from ~2.74 to ~1.75 pts after 2020, Pelechrinis 2023) - improves held-out log loss by >= 0.003 nats at zero new information.
canonical_model: src/Models/logreg_rolling.py: RollingLogreg (C=1.0, L2, lbfgs) on load_design() features resolved through DEFAULT_MODELS['full'] (22 contrast columns incl. home_adv). Measured pooled OOF log loss 0.61957 on 6,600 rows / 5 splits (walk_forward_split(n_splits=5, initial_frac=0.5, gap=0)), reproduced in this session before pre-registration. The model is NOT refit, retuned or re-featured by this experiment: OOF probabilities are produced once and calibrated post-hoc.
prior_evidence: results/round3_calib.jsonl already found nested calibrators a null on the E14 frame (temperature -0.0005, platt -0.0008, beta -0.0008, isotonic -0.0080 worse; all intervals straddle zero or worse). That run differs in (i) model/frame (43-col E14, ll 0.618307), (ii) calibrator fit slice (inner 3-split walk-forward OOF inside the outer training rows), (iii) no regime variant. The prior is AGAINST H3; this run tests the season-blocked slicing and the home-regime parameterisation the dossier names. Not a repeat of a tested setup.

protocol.oof: Canonical walk-forward, 5 splits, initial_frac 0.5, gap 0. One OOF probability per row, produced BEFORE any calibration. The fold model's home_adv coefficient h_i is recorded per row (needed by variant c).
protocol.fit_slices: For scored block S, each fitted calibrator is fit on the OOF rows of the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING season block S-1 ONLY. The labels of S are never seen by the calibrator that scores S. The first block (2020-21 tail) has no in-region predecessor and passes through IDENTITY for every fitted variant. Stated explicitly because this is the failure mode the repo documents (the original pipeline fit its calibrator on the same tail used for early stopping and validation): NO calibrator in this run ever fits and scores the same rows, and no calibrator ever sees a label from the block it scores.

variants.isotonic_prevseason: sklearn IsotonicRegression(out_of_bounds='clip', y_min=1e-4, y_max=1-1e-4) fit on (p, y) of block S-1, applied to block S.
variants.platt_prevseason: p' = sigmoid(a*logit(p) + b); (a,b) from unpenalised logistic (C=1e6) on block S-1.
variants.home_regime_shrink: z'_i = z_i - (1 - rho)*h_i with rho = 1.75/2.74 = 0.6387 FIXED ex ante from Pelechrinis (2023) (ratio of post-2020 to pre-2020 home margin in points, applied to the home log-odds term under an assumed stable margin->logit scale); h_i = the home_adv coefficient of the fold model that produced row i, read from the fitted model (the model itself is not refit). ZERO fitted parameters and no fit slice: the canonical model's home term is treated as a regime parameter and shrunk to its post-2020 value. Every scored row is post-2020-03-11, so the shrink applies to all scored rows. Single fixed constant; no sweep over rho.
variants.home_intercept_adj: z'_i = z_i + gamma_S, gamma_S = intercept-only MLE on block S-1 (one parameter; the 'home-probability intercept adjustment' form of the same hypothesis). Decomposes whether any Platt movement lives in slope or intercept.

protocol.metrics: Log loss (primary), Brier, ECE (uniform-10 and quantile-10 via src/Utils/metrics.expected_calibration_error), before/after per variant, pooled over all 6,600 scored rows and per season block. Paired bootstrap (n_boot=2000, seeds 42/137/2718) on loss(before) - loss(after) via nba_data.paired_bootstrap_delta: POSITIVE delta = recalibration improved. SE = (ci_hi - ci_lo)/(2*1.959964); |z| = delta/SE; z against the 0.003 target = (delta - 0.003)/SE.
protocol.decision_rule: H3 succeeds iff some variant reaches pooled improvement >= 0.003 nats (the pre-registered minimum effect) with its 95% CI excluding zero AND |z| > 3 against zero (the Vandenbruaene et al. 2022 bar). Best-of-4 selection cost (best - median, best - worst, in nats) is printed and logged.
protocol.multiplicity: 4 variant looks -> Bonferroni 0.05/4 = 0.0125 one-sided (|z| ~ 2.24). The project's |z| > 3 bar (~0.00135 one-sided) is stricter and governs. The 3 bootstrap seeds do not add looks: they resample the same rows.
protocol.sizing: SE ~= 0.00078 nats on all-sample features; |z| > 3 needs ~0.0024 nats; pre-registered minimum effect 0.003 nats.

name: H4-prereg-relative-rest
hypothesis: The schedule block's sub-bar effect (delta -0.00204 nats in feature_block_ablation's minus-block convention, localised to back-to-backs by the issue #45 decomposition) is mis-parameterised: rest should enter as the REST-DAY DIFFERENTIAL between the two teams (relative rest; Esteves et al. 2021 found relative rest matters more than absolute), not as team-wise absolute day counts. A relative-rest block should show >= 0.0024 nats and the home/away B2B columns should shrink when it is present.

candidate_block.name: relative_rest
candidate_block.built_from: rest_and_travel() outputs (home_rest_days, away_rest_days, home_back_to_back, away_back_to_back) - the existing schedule data. load_design and the canonical frame are NOT modified; the candidate is new derived columns, registered as its own block and scored by ablation.
candidate_block.definitions: r_side = clip(rest_days, 1, 4) ('capped at ~4+ days'; also kills the October season-indicator artifact the raw column carries). rest_diff_cap4 = r_home - r_away in [-3, 3]. b2b_diff = home_back_to_back - away_back_to_back in [-1, 1] (nonzero exactly when one side is on a B2B and the other is not). Esteves-style relative-rest factor as dummies on d = rest_diff_cap4 with equal rest (d==0) as reference: rel_rest_d_le_m2 (d <= -2), rel_rest_d_m1 (d == -1), rel_rest_d_p1 (d == +1), rel_rest_d_ge_p2 (d >= +2). Pre-declared caveat: the continuous diff and the factor dummies are collinear by construction; the block is scored as ONE unit and no per-column attribution is claimed.
candidate_block.registry: Registered as its own block in feature_block_ablation.FEATURE_BLOCKS under NEW column names (differentials, not the absolute rest columns), so test_blocks_do_not_overlap holds: the schedule block keeps home_rest_days/away_rest_days/home_back_to_back/away_back_to_back/home_in_3_of_4/away_in_3_of_4/travel_miles and nothing moves between blocks. build_feature_frame emits the six candidate columns (new feature-block code, same style as league_rank_features). The H4 arms below pin the canonical 67-column base EXPLICITLY (frame minus the 6 candidate columns) so every comparison runs against the historical instrument's frame, unchanged in columns and order.

arms: A1 = canonical 67-col frame (build_feature_frame output minus the 6 candidate columns, identical to the historical frame). A2 = A1 + candidate (73 cols). A3 = A2 minus the schedule block's 7 columns (66 cols).
comparisons: C1 = A2 vs A1 ('full + candidate vs full'): does relative rest earn its place. C2 = A3 vs A1 ('full + candidate minus schedule vs full'): can relative rest replace absolute rest and still beat the canonical frame. C3 = A3 vs A2 (SUPPLEMENTARY, primary setting only): does dropping absolute rest once the candidate is present cost anything - the direct 'replace' test. Sign convention on every row: delta = loss(first arm) - loss(second arm) via nba_data.paired_bootstrap_delta(y, p_first, p_second); POSITIVE delta means the SECOND arm is better. C1/C2 use A1 as first arm; C3 uses A2. Note feature_block_ablation's minus-block convention has the opposite helpful sign (schedule's historical -0.00204): magnitudes are comparable, signs are not, and each row names its own convention.
settings: Primary: bootstrap seed 42 / 5 folds (n_boot 2000). Replications: bootstrap seeds 137 and 2718 at 5 folds, and 8 folds at seed 42. Attributed honestly (per the issue #45 erratum): walk_forward_split and the lbfgs fit are seed-invariant, so at a fixed fold count the point delta is identical across bootstrap seeds by construction and the seed dimension probes CI variability only; the 8-fold setting is the real replication. Signs 'consistent across replications' is therefore a real requirement only across the fold settings.
secondary_diagnostic: Standardised |coef| of home_back_to_back / away_back_to_back / home_rest_days / away_rest_days in A1 vs A2 (primary setting, per fold and mean): the pre-registered expectation is that home_back_to_back/away_back_to_back SHRINK when the relative-rest block is present. Descriptive; no test, no look.
decision_rule: The rest-differential block earns its place iff (a) the primary C1 CI excludes zero in the helpful direction (delta > 0), (b) |z| > 3 at the primary setting, and (c) the sign is consistent (delta > 0) across every replication setting. C2 answers the replacement question and is judged against the same bar but does not enter the earn-its-place verdict. Minimum effect of interest 0.0024 nats (|z| > 3 at SE ~ 0.0008).
multiplicity: 9 looks for the H4 family: C1 x 4 settings + C2 x 4 settings + C3 x 1 -> Bonferroni 0.05/9 = 0.00556 one-sided (|z| ~ 2.54). H3's 4 looks are a separate family (0.0125). The project's |z| > 3 bar governs on top. No threshold sweeps and no selection among column subsets: the block is fixed here, before it is measured.
prior_evidence: The issue #45 decomposition localised the schedule block's effect to home_back_to_back (-0.00079, CI [-0.00137, -0.00023]) with away_back_to_back leaning the same way (-0.00092, straddles zero); both absolute rest_days and both in_3_of_4 were nulls. That is the evidence that the differential parameterisation is worth testing. Against it: every rest reweighting in this repo so far (recency windows, decay speeds) has been a null.

name: H11-prereg-absence-context
experiment_type: feature-block candidate (theory dossier H11): role-substitution / usage redistribution
hypothesis: An absence-context block improves held-out log loss by >= 0.002 nats INCREMENTALLY on top of the canonical frame + the existing availability block (expected minutes of the prior-game squad; measured +0.0038 nats [0.0023, 0.0055]), with the 95% CI excluding zero and |z| > 3. The availability block says HOW MUCH is missing; H11 asks whether WHAT KIND of missing value is being absorbed adds anything on top (star-absence vs diffuse absence, how the team has historically played without that player, and the remaining squad's next-man-up capacity).

candidate_block.name: absence_context
candidate_block.size_note: 6 columns <= the pre-registered cap; the square / 'top-1 vs spread' dummy named in the dossier is DROPPED to respect it (docs/modeling_exploration.md: the 66-col play-type PPP block).

definitions.presumed_missing_set: M(i) = {players with >= 2 appearances in the team's trailing 10 team-games strictly before game i} minus the prior-game squad (players who appeared in the team's previous game). 'A player who was in the recent rotation and did not play' - never tonight's participants.
definitions.usage_minutes: u_p(i) = (trailing EWMA of USG_PCT, halflife 15) x (trailing EWMA of MIN, halflife 15), carried forward from p's most recent appearance strictly before i. Shift-within-player via nba_data._ewm_by_player.
definitions.g1_{side}_missing_usage_share: u of the highest-u presumed-missing player / total u of the rotation; 0.0 if nobody is presumed missing; NaN only for a team's first game on record.
definitions.g2_{side}_margin_without_missing_top: exponentially weighted mean (weights 0.5^(team-games ago/10), normalised over qualifying games - the repo's NaN-masked ewm convention) of the team's margin over the past 40 team-games in which that player was absent (and already established on the team); shrunk w = n/(n+5) toward rolling_team_features' ewm_margin (consumed, not redefined); with nobody missing the value IS that EWMA.
definitions.g3_{side}_margin_without_top2_usage: same construction over past games missing at least one of the team's current top-2 u players (appearance in the trailing 20 team-games). 'without any of its top-2' is pre-registered as 'missing at least one of the two': both-out games are thin enough that the estimator would fall back to overall form almost everywhere.

causal_convention: Pre-game information only. The prior-game squad is the availability proxy (availability_features' own membership: players with a player_minutes row in the team's previous game). name: H1H2-prereg-market-anchor
experiment_type: market-anchored blend (theory Batch A gate-keepers H1 and H2): does the basketball information add anything the closing price does not already contain?

hypothesis.H1a_primary: The walk-forward logistic stack of [price logit, canonical-model logit] (P+M) beats the de-vigged closing price alone (P) by >= 0.002 nats held-out log loss, with the paired-bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero and |z| > 3. This is THE alpha question: is any of our information not already in the close?
hypothesis.H1b_descriptive: P+M beats the model alone (M) - expected large (the market alone beats M by 0.0227 nats, |z| 7.28 on the 5,788-game overlap). No decision weight: it shows the blend machinery works.
hypothesis.H2_primary: Replacing the plain model logit with the model+availability logit (P+M+A) beats P+M by >= 0.002 nats, CI excluding zero, |z| > 3. Is the availability block's signal already priced by the close? Dare et al. (2015) found player absence fully priced at the close on 1995-2012 data; the NBA changed its injury-report rules in Dec 2025, so this is genuinely open on this data.

odds_role_note: The closing line is a PRE-TIP-OFF quantity and is legitimate as an INPUT for outcome prediction here. The project's 'odds are never a feature' rule governs the MARKET-EVALUATION models (betting/ROI arms) only. On record so the distinction cannot be quietly re-litigated later.

arms.P: de-vigged closing probability (proportional de-vig, closing_line.join_odds' p_market)
arms.M: canonical model OOF home-win probability, load_design(with_availability=False) + the OOF machinery of closing_line.model_probs (walk_forward_split, 5 splits)
arms.M+A: the same with with_availability=True (the project's one confirmed mechanism; pooled OOF log loss 0.61566)
arms.P+M+A: logistic stack of [logit(P), logit(M+A)] - the 'model+availability logit in place of the plain one' parameterization, FIXED here ex ante. The residualized availability variant is declared NOT run (no parameterization selection).

de_vig: PROPORTIONAL, fixed ex ante (Kelly_Criterion devig_two_way(method='proportional'), identical to join_odds' p_market up to rounding). Shin's de-vig is declared NOT run: choosing the de-vig after seeing which one flatters the model is selection.
stacking_protocol: Strictly walk-forward BY SEASON BLOCK. Scored seasons 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, 2025-26; the overlap's first season (2020-21, 460 rows) is the initial training block and is NOT scored. For scored season k the stack is fit on every overlap row of the seasons before k (expanding window) and scores k only. Features logit(p) = log(p/(1-p)) with p clipped to [1e-6, 1-1e-6] as in nba_data.evaluate. Pipeline StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C=1.0, max_iter=300, random_state=42); imputation is unnecessary (all logits finite by construction) and the scaler + estimator are fit on train blocks only. Train/test disjointness is ASSERTED on season labels and on dates (max train date < min test date). Identical scored rows across arms are ASSERTED (single scored frame, all-arm finite).
comparisons: delta = loss(first arm) - loss(second arm); POSITIVE = the second arm is better (nba_data.paired_bootstrap_delta's convention, stated in every row). H1a: loss(P) - loss(P+M). H1b: loss(M) - loss(P+M). H2: loss(P+M) - loss(P+M+A).
decision_rule: H1a succeeds iff delta >= 0.002 nats (the pre-registered minimum effect), the 95% CI excludes zero in the helpful direction, AND |z| > 3. H2 is governed by the same rule on its own delta. Otherwise: 'sub-bar lead' if the CI excludes zero with |z| <= 3; 'null' if the CI straddles zero; 'priced / market better' if the CI excludes zero against the candidate. A null is a complete and valuable result. H1b is descriptive only.
multiplicity: 3 primary looks (H1a, H1b, H2) -> Bonferroni 0.05/3 = 0.0167 one-sided (|z| ~ 2.13). The project bar |z| > 3 governs on top. The bootstrap seeds do not add looks (same rows resampled). Per-season deltas, the stacking-weight drift table and the residual diagnostic are descriptive, carry no decision weight and add no looks.
settings: Primary: bootstrap seed 42 (n_boot 2000). Replications: seeds 137 and 2718. The stack fits and the walk-forward splits are deterministic (lbfgs, fixed random_state), so the seed dimension probes CI variability only; deltas are expected identical across seeds and any non-identity is itself a bug signal.
metrics: Primary: held-out log loss on the scored rows. Also Brier, ROC-AUC, accuracy and the nba_data.evaluate calibration table per arm; SE = (ci_hi - ci_lo)/(2*1.959964); |z| = delta/SE. Per-season log-loss deltas for every hypothesis (season drift read). Stacking-weight drift: walk-forward (train) weights vs a diagnostic-only refit on the scored block (NEVER used for scoring) - do the weights drift, is the model weight ~ 0 in later seasons?
sizing: SE on this overlap is ~0.0015-0.002 nats for a paired log-loss delta; the pre-registered minimum effect (0.002 nats) sits AT or below |z| ~ 1-1.5 at that SE, so this design can only confirm effects meaningfully larger than 0.002 nats (~0.005-0.006 at the wide end of the SE range). A null at 0.002 nats therefore does NOT establish that there is nothing there - it establishes nothing at the bar. This power caveat is fixed before the run.
causal_convention: Everything used to score a game is derived from information strictly before it: the closing line is pre-tip-off; the model logits are OUT-OF-FOLD from walk_forward_split (each block's model trained on games strictly before the block); the stack for a scored season is fit only on earlier seasons' rows and labels. Availability is the prior-game squad's expected minutes (never tonight's participants).
leakage_checks_asserted_in_code: (1) ALIGNMENT: the pipeline must reproduce results/closing_line.json on the 5,788-game overlap (market 0.597657, model 0.623398, model+availability 0.620339) within 1e-6 or it raises - the searchsorted misalignment failure mode. prior_evidence: AGAINST our alpha: the market beats the canonical model by 0.0257 nats |z| 8.18 and beats model+availability by 0.0227 nats |z| 7.28 (results/closing_line.json); Vandenbruaene et al. 2022 found no post-correction profitability across 628 implementations. FOR even trying: a blend can add a little even when each arm alone loses, and the availability block is the project's one confirmed mechanism (+0.0038 nats over the model) whose increment beyond the PRICE has never been measured. Dare et al. 2015 (absence fully priced, 1995-2012) is the prior for H2's null; the Dec 2025 NBA injury-report rule change is the reason it is re-opened.

name: C44-prereg-spread-total
experiment_type: Batch C (issue #44): pre-registered measurement of margin-distribution models on the spread and total markets

hypothesis.C1_pace_first: A pace-first decomposition (possessions first, then points-per-possession per side; margin and total derived from the same two team-point predictions) beats the monolithic margin/total ridge on BOTH margin RMSE and total RMSE over identical walk-forward test rows: delta > 0, 95% CI excluding zero, |z| > 3. Baseline is margin_total run as-is (its documented 14.01 / 18.78 must reproduce).
hypothesis.C2_distributional_margin: A proper margin distribution beats Phi(mhat/sigma): the SKELLAM on (mu_home, mu_away) = ((t_hat+m_hat)/2, (t_hat-m_hat)/2) from margin_total's own predictions - integer-valued like a margin, game-specific variance mu_h+mu_a = predicted total, zero additional fitted parameters - scores better than the single-scale Gaussian on (a) the margin-bucket log score (>= 0.002 nats, CI excluding zero, |z| > 3) OR (b) cover-probability calibration against the closing spread (cover log-loss delta, CI excluding zero, |z| > 3). Total-over probabilities vs the closing total are scored and reported but carry no decision weight.

arms.baseline: margin_total.MarginTotalModel() with default parameters (alpha auto, sigma oof, poisson auto), fit per walk-forward split on training rows only, module unmodified.
arms.C1: pace_first.PaceFirstModel() (3 ridges: possessions, home ppp, away ppp), same folds, same ridge grid and the same inner-CV selector imported from margin_total.
arms.C2: Skellam(mu_home, mu_away) over the baseline's (m_hat, t_hat) vs the baseline's own N(m_hat, sigma^2). The comparison isolates distribution form: same means, same folds, same rows.
arms.named_not_run: quantile / dispersion model (Gaussian margin with a predicted per-game scale); Skellam over the C1 arm's team points; any threshold sweep. Not run: each is an extra fitted dispersion layer and/or an extra look.

parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.splits: nba_data.walk_forward_split(n_splits=5, initial_frac=0.5, gap=0); identical rows across every arm
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.features: the shared causal builders only (nba_data.rolling_team_features halflife 10 min_games 5, nba_data.rest_and_travel); pace_first.possessions_target is an outcome-derived TRAINING TARGET (Dean Oliver box-score possessions), never a feature
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.skellam_rates: mu = clip((t_hat +/- m_hat)/2, 0.01, None); t_hat = margin_total predict_total_gaussian, m_hat = predict_margin
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.margin_buckets: primary: exact integer margin (bucket = one point; Gaussian arm scores Phi((k+0.5-m)/sigma) - Phi((k-0.5-m)/sigma), Skellam arm scores its pmf at k); robustness (no decision weight): 5-point buckets [5j-2.5, 5j+2.5]
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.cover_rule: cover iff margin > L_eff; K = floor(L_eff)+1; P(cover) = P(margin >= K) under each arm's own distribution; pushes (margin == L_eff) excluded, counted
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.L_eff: 2022-23..2025-26: Spread (signed expected home margin). 2015-16..2021-22: unsigned favourite handicap - +Spread if the home side is the de-vigged moneyline favourite else -Spread. Fixed from the inventory cover-rate diagnostics before any arm ran
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.market_rows: walk-forward test rows with a closing line, |Spread| <= 40.0, OU in [150.0, 290.0]; identical rows across arms
parameterization_fixed_ex_ante.roi_rule: closing_line.roi() reused with threshold=0.5 at a flat p_raw = 110/210: bet the side the model makes more likely whenever its probability beats the posted price; both sides considered; no free threshold; stake = edge over the price (roi()'s own convention)

metrics: C1: pooled per-game margin RMSE and total RMSE (delta vs baseline, paired bootstrap over games, 2000 resamples) + per-split means for parity with 14.01/18.78 + MAE. C2 (a): per-game margin log score (log loss in nats) on identical rows. C2 (b): cover log loss + Brier + 10-bin calibration/ECE for both arms. Secondary: 5-point-bucket log score, total-over log loss and calibration, per-season breakdowns of every primary endpoint, spread/total MAE and RMSE vs the closing line as a forecaster, ROI. SE = (ci_hi-ci_lo)/(2*1.959964); |z| = delta/SE.

decision_rule.C1: succeeds iff BOTH margin-RMSE and total-RMSE deltas are > 0 with 95% CI excluding zero and |z| > 3 at the primary setting (seed 42, 5 folds), with the sign stable at seeds 137 and 2718. Otherwise 'sub-bar lead' (CI excludes zero, |z| <= 3) or 'null' (CI straddles zero).
decision_rule.C2: succeeds iff (a) margin-log-score delta >= 0.002 nats with CI excluding zero and |z| > 3, OR (b) cover-log-loss delta > 0 with CI excluding zero and |z| > 3, at the primary setting, sign stable at the replication seeds.
decision_rule.market: an ROI at |z| > 3 would be a finding; the prior is efficient (ROI <= 0). A null is a complete result.

multiplicity: 6 looks in the Batch C family (C1 x 2, C2 x 2, market ROI x 2) -> Bonferroni 0.05/6 = 0.0083 one-sided. The |z| > 3 bar (~0.00135 one-sided) is stricter and governs. Replication seeds resample the same rows and add no looks; secondary metrics cannot promote a result.
leakage_plan: All features strictly pre-tip-off via the shared causal builders (shift-within-team, truncation-invariant). Every fitted quantity (imputer, scaler, ridge penalty and coefficients, sigma, sigma_total, the Poisson fit) is fit on TRAIN rows only, inside the walk-forward loop; dispersion parameters are train-only by construction and the Skellam arm fits NOTHING beyond them. The odds columns (Spread/OU/ML) are used only as market lines and prices to score against, never as features; the odds tables' own outcome columns (Points/Win_Margin) are never consumed - outcomes come from nba_data.build_games. Identical scored rows across arms is asserted in code.
runtime_note: Both arms fit per fold with inner CV; roughly 5-15 minutes total, cached under /tmp/opencode/c44/. No search, no sweep, no variants - selection cost is zero because nothing is selected.

experiment_type: new model class: feed-forward neural network on the canonical 26-feature frame (Pipeline A)

fixed_ex_ante.decision_rule: Promotion requires a positive seed-averaged delta with |z| > 3 on 2,000 paired bootstrap resamples (seed 42). A single favourable seed cannot promote: the decision is the pre-registered seed-average. Any other outcome is reported as a null or a negative result with its interval, not as a near-miss.
fixed_ex_ante.delta: loss(reference) - loss(candidate); positive means the neural network is better.
fixed_ex_ante.frame: logreg_rolling.load_design() restricted to logreg_rolling.resolve_features(DEFAULT_MODELS['full']): the 26 canonical columns, in their canonical order, including the four availability columns. No feature is added, dropped or re-derived for this arm.
fixed_ex_ante.population: every row of build_games() (13,199 games). The five walk-forward splits are nba_data.walk_forward_split(n_splits=5, initial_frac=0.5), so the first 50% of games are train-only and the last 50% are five contiguous test blocks; 6,600 rows are scored. Row order is the build_games() order and is never re-sorted.
fixed_ex_ante.preprocessing: logreg_rolling.FeaturePipeline(columns=features), fitted separately on each training block and never on the test block: per-column training median imputation, then training mean/sd z-scoring, with home_adv passed through unscaled as in the canonical model. The reference model uses the same class and contract.
fixed_ex_ante.primary_arm: the mean predicted probability of five MLPs fitted with seeds 42, 43, 44, 45 and 46 on each training block. Seed averaging is part of the pre-registered arm, not a post-hoc choice: neural network fits are seed-sensitive and the arm must not depend on one lucky initialisation.
fixed_ex_ante.reference: the canonical model: RollingLogreg(C=1.0) on the same 26 columns, same FeaturePipeline, same folds, via measurement.canonical_oof. The recorded post-#36 pooled OOF log loss is 0.615663649; the run reports the reproduced value and its drift rather than assuming it.
fixed_ex_ante.reporting: Absolute log loss, Brier, AUC and accuracy for the reference and the primary arm; the paired delta with CI and |z|; every fold; every seed's own OOF delta; and every sensitivity configuration, including ones that lose. The result is written to results/nn_rolling.json and .md and appended to results/experiments.jsonl.
fixed_ex_ante.scope: This arm answers one question: does this pre-registered MLP beat the canonical logistic on this frame and these folds? It does not answer whether some other neural architecture, a Keras deep net, or a tuned network could. No architecture search is run on the test blocks.

sensitivity.why: Descriptive robustness only. These configurations cannot promote and are not candidates for the headline: choosing one after reading the test block would be architecture shopping.

hypothesis: A feed-forward multilayer perceptron can learn non-linear interactions between the 26 causal team-form, schedule and availability features that the L2-penalised canonical logistic regression cannot represent. If those interactions carry signal, the MLP will beat the canonical model on the identical walk-forward rows by a positive loss(canonical) - loss(MLP) at |z| > 3. The prior is against it: on this frame XGBoost and HistGradientBoosting both lost to the canonical model by about 0.0079 nats, and the one proven feature block is a linear expected-minutes adjustment.
